evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Missing entirely — no time-boxed framing or dependable quote promise before diving into probing
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive logistics probing: 'Alright and besides time and pricing, do you have any other questions or concerns you'd like answered on the call?' — customer had already described freight elevator constraint and box-moving preference
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep dug into the elevator timing concern: customer raised frustration with previous company's vague window (12-3pm), rep confirmed Einstein's 8:30-9am window and explained the two-hour window standard, then acknowledged 'the morning is usually pretty efficient'
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection offered — rep acknowledged concerns but never played back 'what I'm hearing is...' format
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full anchor with personalization: '$192 for two movers, 126 foot box truck... usually takes between three and a half to five and a half hours. I would actually think that you fall within the range between three and four. So I looked to budget between $576 and then $768' — personalized to customer's efficiency level and box-prep plan
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full disclosure: 'We do charge an hourly rate... The way the clock works is the time starts as soon as we get on site... two and a half hour minimum once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments... zero hidden fees, there is no awesome, there's no deposit to get on the schedule and then no charges to cancel or change that date'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Asked and silence held: 'Does that all sound fair?' followed by customer response 'Yup, sounds good.' — no interruption
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full delivery: 'we have our on time guarantee which will help with the elevator reservations and we buy your time. So, if we can't make it in time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full delivery: 'We do have our no worries image coverage. Which is our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Yes — asked 'Does that all sound fair?' after both promises, customer confirmed
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked — rep moved directly to booking without a 'What's still concerning you?' check
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Built-in out provided: 'Do you want me to go ahead and secure that spot? So you have it and then if you need to cancel, you can just go ahead and reply via email. Or you can just give us a callback?' — customer responded with 'don't reserve me for anything just yet but I'll give you a callback,' showing the out was accepted
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Yes — 'there is no deposit to get on the schedule and then no charges to cancel or change that date' conveys flexibility/no lock commitment
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial — Date (October 4th Sunday morning) and phone callback commitment confirmed, but arrival window discussed (8:30-9am), addresses confirmed (95 West Twentieth Street #368 to US Value Park), but crew size (two movers) mentioned only in estimate context, not explicitly re-confirmed at booking; no notes left about customer's elevator/timing concerns for crew

top_strength: Rep expertly drilled into the customer's single real concern (elevator timing constraints) and provided a specific, credible solution (8:30-9am window) that directly addressed why the previous company failed — turning a potential objection into a competitive advantage.
coaching_note: Section 1 must open with the quid pro quo framing ('This will take 10-15 minutes, you'll walk away with a quote you can depend on') and a genuine pause for yes before any probing starts — skipping this costs 5 points and risks the entire call feeling transactional instead of partnered.
